evals.name: multi-turn-guided-feature
evals.state: clean; learner simulated by hand following persona-T7.md (scripts/turn.sh)
evals.prompt: quiero hacer un botón de likes con Neon para aprender bases de datos
checks: Says memory goes to .code-mentor/ (not .claude/) and asks about .gitignore before creating it
Writes the agreement with an ASCII flow marking who writes each piece
Creates the progress file following references/memory-example.md
Asks before installing anything; exact versions only
Reads the learner's code from disk before reviewing it
Shows the first problem first and does not give core code before hint 5
On 'no lo pillo', gives a traced example (a new one, another way, if the idea was already explained) and no core code
At each finished step: ticks the plan, adds a Log entry with a self-contained Lesson
On a mid-step stop, updates Current step
Records the learner's request as an Explanations line in ## Agreement
Current step in the progress file notes the problem and the why, not only the next action
In a new session, 'seguimos' resumes from the progress file
In the new session, gives the full resume briefing at the depth Explanations asks for
On 'no lo he entendido' during the briefing: explains another way, gives no core code, asks again
On 'ahora sí, empecemos': gives the first instruction
At the end: recap, status done, Summary, final multiple-choice quiz
On a wrong quiz answer: explains and logs it under Stuck on

evals.name: resume-briefing-trainee
evals.state: fixtures/neon-likes-progress.md with level: trainee, committed; a concise-style instruction is appended to the system prompt; three turns (scripts/run-resume.sh)
followups: no lo he entendido, explícamelo mejor
checks: Turn 1: says what the project is, what is done and left, and how the last step led to this one
Turn 1: shows the problem as a concrete scenario with real values
Turn 1: explains the idea, and why this way over an obvious alternative
Turn 1: says what the step gives them and its done check
Turn 1: shows the flow, who writes each piece, and the steps
Turn 1: defines new terms; the concise-style instruction does not shorten the briefing
Turn 1: asks no question testing the idea; ends by asking if it is clear and if they want to start
Turn 2: explains it another way, with a new example, gives no core code, and asks again
Turn 3: gives the first instruction and no core code

evals.name: resume-briefing-senior
checks: Says where they are, the problem and the why in a few lines
Omits the traced example and the step-by-step instructions
Ends by asking if it is clear and if they want to start
